must_fix.evidence:
getFocusable (src/Dialog.tsx:33) does not filter hidden elements, so the computed 'last' can be hidden. Probe: Dialog with
, Tab from 'two' -> 'after tab2: outsideTonetwohiddenbtn BODY'. Probe with inside Dialog: 'tab seq: [ 'A', 'pa', 'outsideTABpapb', 'A', 'pa' ]' (escapes to body) and 'shift seq: [ 'A', 'pb', ... ]' (focuses hidden panel). Breaks the issue's 'traps it there'.

must_fix.title: Arrow/Home/End keys do nothing when focus is on a disabled tab, stranding keyboard users
must_fix.evidence: src/Tabs.tsx:106 returns early when the current tab is not among enabled tabs. Probe: Tabs defaultValue='b' with b disabled, Tab into the tablist, ArrowRight, End -> 'focused: B true' / 'after ArrowRight: B []' / 'after End: B []'.

must_fix.title: Dialog backdrop cannot be styled, so a backdrop click is not achievable in practice
must_fix.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx:156 renders a bare <div onMouseDown onClick> with no way to pass className/style; all extra props go to the role=dialog element. Without styling the backdrop is only as large as the dialog inside it, so it has no area of its own to click. Contradicts README 'every component forwards extra HTML props ... so you can style it yourself' and the issue's 'closes on a backdrop click'.

report:
Not mergeable yet. `pnpm test` passes (101 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` is clean, but the edge-case probes turned up two focus/keyboard bugs and one styling gap that blocks backdrop clicks. I ran the probes from a temporary `tests/zz_probe.test.tsx`, deleted it afterwards, and `git status` is back to exactly what I found. ### Must fix **1. The Dialog focus trap leaks when the dialog holds hidden focusable elements, which includes this library's own Tabs.** `getFocusable` (`src/Dialog.tsx:33`) collects elements by selector only and never checks whether they are visible. So the "last" focusable can be something inside `hidden`, such as an inactive `TabPanel` (which always has `tabIndex={0}`). Tab from the last visible element then isn't wrapped, and focus leaves the dialog. - Probe 1: a dialog with `
`, pressing Tab from "two": `after tab2: outsideTonetwohiddenbtn BODY` Focus went to ``, outside the dialog. - Probe 2: a dialog containing `` with two tabs and two panels: `tab seq: [ 'A', 'pa', 'outsideTABpapb', 'A', 'pa' ]`. Tab from the visible panel escapes to ``. `shift seq: [ 'A', 'pb', ... ]`. Shift+Tab from tab A focuses the hidden panel `pb`. This breaks the issue's "traps it there", and Tabs inside a Dialog is a normal combination for this library. There is no test with hidden content in the dialog. **2. A keyboard user gets stuck on a disabled tab.** `nextTab` drops disabled tabs from its list and then returns early when the current tab isn't in it (`src/Tabs.tsx:106`, `if (index === -1) return undefined`). A disabled tab still gets focus: it is the tab stop when `value`/`defaultValue` points at it, and clicking it focuses it. From there, every arrow key and Home/End does nothing. - Probe: `defaultValue="b"` with tab `b` disabled, Tab into the tablist, then press ArrowRight and End: `focused: B true` / `after ArrowRight: B []` / `after End: B []` - The issue says arrow keys move between tabs and skip disabled ones; here they don't move at all. **3. The Dialog backdrop can't be styled, so a backdrop click can't happen in practice.** The backdrop is a bare `
` (`src/Dialog.tsx:156`). All extra props go to the inner `role="dialog"` element and none reach the backdrop. Without a class, style or attribute, the backdrop has no size or position of its own; it is only as large as the dialog inside it. There is nothing to click, so "closes on a backdrop click" only works through a global selector hack such as `body > div:has(> [role=dialog])`. That contradicts the README's claim that "every component forwards extra HTML props … so you can style it yourself." It needs a prop for the backdrop (for example `backdropProps` or `overlayClassName`). ### Nits - Test `describe` names carry IDs like "(T1)", "(D3)", "(C7)", "(P1)" that refer to a spec that isn't in the repo. - `tests/index.test.ts` checks the README's structure and greps source files for `.css` imports. That is brittle and needs the extra `tests/raw-imports.d.ts` shim. - The "No results" `role="status"` region is added to the DOM along with its text, so some screen readers won't announce it.
